mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future dividends and equity prices, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same tightening phase (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% for ≥2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.0% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations, prompting risk-averse investors to sell equities, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 60-day forward returns remain non-negative during all months with ΔCPIAUCSL > +2.0% (p > 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs for three consecutive months indicates a strengthening labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the same 20-day horizon, forward returns are negative in at least 60% of similar labor-market-recovery episodes (rolling 12-month comparison).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of RSAFS (retail sales) to INDPRO (industrial production) exceeds 1.10 for two consecutive months, it suggests robust consumer demand relative to supply capacity, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During analogous demand-supply imbalances, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (≥10.0% month-over-month) followed by a sustained rise in HOUST (housing starts) suggests a supply-side shock that outpaces demand recovery, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥10.0% in month 1 AND HOUST rises for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: Supply-side contraction followed by construction rebound
failure_condition: During analogous supply shocks, 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of cases (rolling 36-month window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals tight labor markets, prompting higher wage growth and equity risk appetite, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over the same horizon, forward returns are negative in >50% of comparable labor-tightening episodes (rolling 24-month comparison).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption) by at least 3% in a quarter, without a corresponding drop in FEDFUNDS, suggests a demand-driven soft landing that temporarily boosts risk sentiment, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls ≥3% in a quarter AND FEDFUNDS remains flat for the quarter
failure_condition: During analogous GDP declines, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4.0% and INDPRO remains flat for two consecutive months, it indicates a labor market adjustment without underlying demand growth, which can trigger a risk-off reaction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND INDPRO unchanged for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In analogous regimes, 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >80% of cases (rolling 12-month window).
